transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally made me agree to come in is that I just... I don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. 

Things like sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even just tinkering out in the woodshop... lately, all of that just feels like a chore. I just keep putting them off.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yes, it did. Um, this has all been going on since the scaffold accident... that happened during a big business readjustment. It's been a little over a year now.
Have these feelings been present continuously since the scaffold accident a little over a year ago?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean, I haven't exactly tracked it day by day, but... it feels like it's been pretty constant since it happened. I just haven't been able to get back into any of my normal routines since then.
Do you feel this loss of interest is mainly about the scaffold accident and business upheaval, or does it feel bigger than that?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. Um... I haven't really thought about whether it's bigger than the accident or not. 

I just know that ever since the scaffolding fell and all that chaos at work happened, I just... I don't have the drive for much of anything anymore. I don't know if the feeling itself is specifically about the accident every time I skip going out to the woodshop, it's just... that's when all this started, and it just hasn't gone away.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel depressed. I don't feel sad or down most days. It's... it's more just that lack of interest I was talking about. I'm just kind of going through the motions right now, but I wouldn't call it feeling depressed.
Before the scaffold accident, had you ever gone through a period where you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy like this?

No, never. I've always been a pretty active guy, you know? I always had some project going in the woodshop or something to keep me busy on the weekends. This is... this is definitely new for me. Before the accident, I never had a problem finding something I wanted to do.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about the normal stuff, like paying the bills and keeping the house up, but... no, I wouldn't say I worry excessively about a bunch of different things. It's just the usual day-to-day stuff.
Has this loss of interest been causing problems in your daily life or work?

Well, it's definitely having an impact at work. I'm still doing my job as a project manager, but... I've started delegating site visits that I really should be leading myself. And I find myself avoiding client discussions if I think they might bring up the accident. It's making me worry that I'm not giving the projects the steady direction they need right now.
Do you go out of your way to avoid reminders of the scaffold accident?

Yes, I do. I've actually gotten very good at routing my day so I don't have to go anywhere near that coastal site. I stay away from the harbor walkways by the cranes, too. And... well, if a conversation starts heading toward someone replaying what went wrong that day, I just find a way to excuse myself. I really don't want to be around any of it.
Do unwanted memories of the scaffold accident keep popping into your mind?

Yeah, they do. Out of nowhere, I'll just... I'll see that scaffold dropping in my head. It's as clear as a photo. It usually happens if I hear a loud metal clank, or maybe a truck's backup alarm. And when that happens, for a few minutes, it's just really hard to stay focused on whatever meeting or conversation I'm actually in.
Have you been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled since the scaffold accident?

Yeah, I have. If someone drops a metal ladder nearby, or maybe a truck gate slams, I just... I jump hard before I can even stop myself. And after it happens, it takes me a lot longer than it should to get my heart rate back down to normal.
Have you been having nightmares about the scaffold accident?
No, I haven't really had any nightmares about it. I mean, my sleep hasn't been perfect, but I'm not waking up from bad dreams about the accident or anything like that.
